**Recommendation: one candidate survives, and it can be killed for free before any GPU.**

The evidence supports exactly one cheap, causally distinct encoder-adaptation mechanism: **function-space step mismatch of the shared recipe**. Identical nominal AdamW 1e-5 on the trunk, global clip 1, standard parametrization, applied to a 768-wide tower with 6 adapted blocks versus a 1024-wide tower with 12 adapted blocks, should move the wide tower's features more per update. If so, "starts stronger, learns less" is under-stepping, not a capacity ceiling. If the saved artifacts show PE's features moved as much as Large's, nothing in the evidence supports another cheap PE encoder-adaptation mechanism and the PE lane should close on capacity grounds. I say that explicitly rather than reinvent a closed rescue.

## Measured basis (from receipts, not new runs)

| Fact | Large/256 | PE-B16/224 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Trainable tensors (blocks + norm + native pool/proj) | 205 | 86 |
| Adapted residual blocks / width | 12 / 1024 | 6 / 768 |
| Pre-clip grad norm median, clipped to 1 every step, scaler fixed 128 | 81.8 | 88.7 |
| Largest trainable gradient group at step 100 | MAP head 0.40 | attn_pool 0.42 |
| Raw1024 held R@1 gain over 100 updates (pp) | +16.51 | +12.01 |
| PE−Large relative raw gain (pp), product 95% | | −4.50 [−5.59, −3.45] |

Clipping is not differential and Adam is scale-invariant, so each arm trains at the Adam-bounded per-parameter step of at most 1e-5. What differs is how much that bounded per-parameter step moves the *function*.

## Causal hypothesis and its falsifier

Under standard parametrization, Adam's per-parameter update is about lr regardless of width, so a layer's output perturbation grows with fan-in and the network's output perturbation grows with the number of adapted residual blocks. μP prescribes Adam hidden-layer LR ∝ 1/width to keep feature updates constant across width (Yang et al. 2022, arXiv:2203.03466); depth-μP adds 1/√L branch scaling for depth transfer (Yang et al. 2023, arXiv:2310.02244; Bordelon et al. 2023, arXiv:2309.16620). Neither is applied in this recipe. First-order projection, conjecture not measurement: Large's per-update feature displacement ≈ (1024/768)·(12/6) ≈ 2.7× PE's, so 100 PE updates would be worth roughly 40 Large updates of function movement. μP theory is derived for from-scratch scaling limits, so I do not trust the multiplier from theory; I measure it.

**F0, CPU, saved artifacts, zero GPU.** The attribution job saved held raw-1024 matrices for encoder0 and encoder100 of both arms (receipt hashes large.0 `0b3969ac…`, large.1 `5238def8…`, pe.0 `151a5091…`, pe.1 `70e7acbf…`). Verify SHAs, then compute per-image angular displacement θ_i = arccos cos(raw0_i, raw100_i) on the same 12,599 held rows, report medians and a paired product bootstrap of the PE/Large median ratio. Predeclare before reading: ALIVE if ratio point ≤ 0.6 and 95% upper < 0.75; DEAD if ratio ≥ 0.85; anything between is inconclusive and closes without threshold search. Cost is seconds and under 1 GiB.

**F1 cross-check, same CPU job.** Per-group ‖θ100−θ0‖_F/‖θ0‖_F from the saved checkpoints against the pinned originals, plus the fraction of the Adam bound lr·100·√n actually used per block. This distinguishes small displacement caused by gradient sign-inconsistency from small displacement caused by the nominal step. Under two minutes, under 8 GiB host.

## Bounded matched arm, only if F0 is ALIVE

One PE arm, trunk LR multiplied by k = Large median θ / PE median θ, clipped to [1.5, 3], fixed before launch. Everything else byte-identical to the frozen pair: seed 179032 first 100 batches, augmented RGB hashes, FP16 autocast with scaler 128, head and proxy LR 1e-4, weight decay 0.05, clip 1, first 6 blocks frozen, own PCA128/proxies/bank. No Large rerun; the frozen control receipt is the comparator.

- Calibration validity, read first: recompute θ on held for the new checkpoint with the existing attribution protocol and require 0.75 ≤ θ_PEk/θ_Large ≤ 1.33. Outside that band the arm is inconclusive and closes, no retune.
- Quality gate, raw1024 held R@1 gain versus the PE baseline gain: advance if ≥ +2.25 pp (half the measured deficit) with paired product-bootstrap lower > 0 and mAP@R gain lower ≥ 0. Kill if < +1.0 pp or lower ≤ 0. PCA128 packed read is secondary and descriptive.
- Resources: one DGX user unit, whole process ≤ 300 s, allocated CUDA < 10 GB, host 8 GiB, cleanup < 8 MiB, all finite and no-skip guards as before. The prior PE arm took 112 s.

Confound separation. Update count is fixed at 100 on identical batches, so any change is per-update efficiency. The trainable set is unchanged, so a pass implicates optimization and a fail with valid calibration implicates capacity or direction. Head and proxy LR are untouched, so the existing 2×2 CPU attribution can re-measure coadaptation. The multiplier is derived once from a measured target with a validity band, which is what separates this from an arbitrary LR sweep; the same logic predicts Large would not benefit, a falsifiable side prediction not run now.

Distinction from closed arms: head-first warmup changed phase order; objective-conflict projection changed gradient direction at the pooler; source MAIN, teacher transfer, sub-center, description, context and augmentation arms changed supervision; freeze16, true-freeze, depth22, cross-depth and multidepth changed which blocks exist or train while every one kept trunk LR 1e-5; rank-32 delta changed update structure; wide, direct256 and nonlinear heads changed readout. The three prior consultations proposed all-TRAIN scaling, sub-centers and a nonlinear head. None measured or matched function-space displacement. No novelty is claimed; μP is prior art and matched displacement is a control.

Rejected alternatives, one line each. Intermediate-layer readout follows the PE paper's title claim (Bolya et al. 2025, arXiv:2504.13181) but is a depth/readout change overlapping closed families. Probe-attention gating through PE's attn_pool is untestable without new forward passes and its fix would be a head change. Unverified: exact trainable parameter counts are inferred from shapes, and the distillation origin of PE-B16 is a model-card claim recorded in the gate, not checked by me.

**Decision.** Run F0/F1 on saved artifacts before any GPU. DEAD or inconclusive closes the PE lane as a capacity result under this recipe. ALIVE licenses exactly one matched-step PE arm under the gate above; passing it authorizes only a separately frozen paired-seed 1,000-update comparison, not official reads or serving claims.
